title: Egg omelet or scrambled egg with dark‑green vegetables, fat added

content.title: About
content.content: The dish consists of eggs prepared as an omelet or scrambled, combined with dark‑green vegetables (such as spinach, broccoli or kale) and a small amount of added fat (butter, olive oil or other). Eggs provide high‑quality protein, while the vegetables are rich in vitamins, minerals and antioxidants.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Dark‑green vegetables contain chlorophyll, giving them their characteristic color and antioxidant properties.
Eggs are one of the few foods that contain all essential amino acids in adequate amounts.
A modest amount of fat improves absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins (A, D, E, K) from the vegetables.
The meal cooks quickly – usually 5‑7 minutes in a pan.
Variations exist worldwide: French "omelette aux épinards", Japanese "tamago to yasai no yaki", etc.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Eggs supply complete protein needed for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Eggs contain B12, riboflavin and biotin, supporting energy metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Vitamins A, C, K and folate
items.content: Dark‑green vegetables provide vitamin A (vision), vitamin C (antioxidant), vitamin K (blood clotting) and folate (cell division).

items.title: Minerals – iron and calcium
items.content: Spinach and broccoli contribute iron and calcium, important for blood and bone health.

items.title: Cardiovascular support
items.content: Monounsaturated fats from the added oil and antioxidants in the vegetables help lower LDL cholesterol.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to egg white proteins.

items.title: Cholesterol content
items.content: Eggs contain cholesterol; people with high cholesterol should consume them in moderation.

items.title: Oxalates in spinach
items.content: Spinach is high in oxalates, which can contribute to kidney stone formation in susceptible persons.

items.title: Over‑heating fat
items.content: Cooking at too high a temperature can produce trans‑fats and harmful compounds.

content.title: How to Cook
content.content: Beat the eggs with a pinch of salt and pepper. Heat 1‑2 tsp of oil in a skillet, add chopped dark‑green vegetables and sauté 2‑3 minutes. Pour the egg mixture over the vegetables and cook, stirring, until the desired consistency is reached (soft omelet or firmer scrambled eggs). Garnish with fresh herbs before serving.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store fresh eggs in the refrigerator for up to 4 weeks. Use vegetables within 2‑3 days, kept in an airtight container in the fridge. Cooked dish should be eaten within 2 hours at room temperature or refrigerated and consumed within 24 hours.
